title: Claims Desk Guidance — When a Claim Is Covered under Northloop Protect Plans
content:
**Rule.** Under the Northloop Protect Plans, a claim is covered only for a failure type listed in the plan's covered failure types, for an incident inside the coverage period after the applicable waiting days, filed within the claim filing window counted from the incident date and, for in-term incidents, no later than the grace days after coverage end. Mechanical failures inside the manufacturer's warranty go to the manufacturer first when the plan's terms send mechanical failures within the manufacturer's warranty period to the manufacturer first. Theft, loss, cosmetic damage, pre-existing conditions and commercial use are never covered. Accident claims are limited to the plan's accident claims per rolling 12 months. Only one claim may be open at a time. A claim of a service-fee failure type is charged the service fee of the item's price band before it is settled.

## Conditions of a covered claim

| Point | What is read on the plan and the claim | Covered only when |
|---|---|---|
| Failure type | What happened to the item | It is one of the plan's covered failure types |
| Incident timing | The incident date against the coverage start and coverage end date | The incident is inside the coverage period and after the waiting days that apply to its failure type |
| Filing | The date the claim is filed against the incident date and the coverage end date | Filed within the claim filing window counted from the incident date and, for an in-term incident, no later than the grace days after coverage end |
| Excluded causes | The cause of the failure | Never theft, loss, cosmetic damage, a pre-existing condition or commercial use |
| Accident allowance | Accident claims already counted on the plan | Within the plan's allowance of accident claims per rolling 12 months |
| Open claims | Other claims open on the plan | No other claim is open |

Mechanical failures inside the manufacturer's warranty go to the manufacturer first on a plan whose terms say so, and a claim of a failure type that carries the service fee is charged the fee of the covered item's price band before the claim is settled.

## Counting accident claims

An accident claim is a claim for accidental damage, liquid damage or a cracked screen. For a new accident claim, the count is the number of the plan's claims that are approved or fulfilled, are for accidental damage, liquid damage or a cracked screen, and have an incident date inside the rolling 12 months ending on the incident date of the new claim. Submitted, denied or withdrawn claims are not counted. The allowance per plan:

| Plan | Approved accident claims allowed in any rolling 12 months |
|---|---|
| Protect 1-Year Extended Warranty | Not applicable (no accident cover) |
| Protect 2-Year Extended Warranty | Not applicable (no accident cover) |
| Protect 3-Year Extended Warranty | Not applicable (no accident cover) |
| Protect 2-Year Accident Protection | 2 |
| Protect 3-Year Accident Protection | 2 |
| Protect 4-Year Accident Protection | 3 |

## Hypothetical cases

| Case | Facts (hypothetical) | Judgement |
|---|---|---|
| A | Protect 2-Year Accident Protection; approved accidental damage claim with incident date 2025-11-03 and fulfilled cracked screen claim with incident date 2026-04-20; new liquid damage incident on 2026-09-01 | Two accident claims fall in the rolling 12 months ending 2026-09-01; the allowance of 2 is used, so the new accident claim is not covered |
| B | As case A, but the first claim's incident date is 2025-06-10 | Only one counted claim falls in the window; the new claim is within the allowance |
| C | As case A, but the 2026-04-20 claim was denied | A denied claim is not counted; the new claim is within the allowance |
| D | A plan with one claim still submitted and a second incident reported | Only one claim may be open at a time |
| E | A phone stolen from a car | Theft is never covered |
